correctness.rationale: Degree-two endpoint parity forces four distinct colors on the first two rungs. At each later degree-three vertex two preexisting distinct neighbor colors preclude any repetition under the odd-multiplicity rule, propagating exactly the graph-square inequalities. The converse is immediate; counting permitted next-rung ordered pairs gives (k-3)^2-(k-4), independently of history. k<4, n=2 and optimum k=4 boundaries are checked. Exhaustive 1,647,568-coloring and 105 independent transfer cases corroborate without replacing the proof.

The claw-free equality theorem is inapplicable to ladders with at least three rungs, and the product theorem is only a bound. The standard ladder chromatic polynomial counts a different class. An inaccessible subsequent study and unindexed equivalents remain possible risks.

value.rationale: The strong odd condition permits monochromatic triples at cubic neighborhoods, so equality with square coloring is substantive for ladders with induced claws. This theorem provides a full palette polynomial, a sharp four-color threshold, and a globally rigid 24-coloring optimal pattern independent of length; the published Cartesian-product bound and ordinary ladder polynomial do not supply these consequences. The family is a natural Cartesian product, not an arbitrary slice.
